title: Connecting the Dots with Context Graphs — Stephen Chin, Neo4j

primary.label: Context Engineering & Memory

summary: Stephen Chin, head of developer relations at Neo4j, presents context graphs as the solution to a core problem in AI-driven enterprise applications: agents lack connected context and lose the reasoning behind past decisions. He opens with a Matrix metaphor — engineers are trapped by AI tools that review their work, and must choose between siloed, disparate knowledge (blue pill) or connected reasoning systems (red pill). Gartner has officially added context graphs to its AI hype cycle, and Foundation Capital published a $3 trillion startup opportunity post about the technology. Chin explains knowledge graphs as structures holding nodes (people, things, companies), relationships, properties, and vector embeddings. Combining LLM strengths (language, reasoning, creativity) with knowledge graph strengths (knowledge, context, enrichments) enables finding hidden patterns and gaining insights. A healthcare example demonstrates the progression: asking about a patient's emphysema care plan, a baseline LLM gives generic advice, vector RAG adds slightly more context but remains generic (respiratory therapy, deep breathing), while graph RAG produces grounded recommendations (medication management, smoking cessation counseling, pulmonary rehabilitation) that reflect the patient's actual history of smoking and prior surgery — information lost in similarity search. Chin identifies three memory types essential for agents: short-term memory (current pipeline state), long-term memory (aggregated domain knowledge across interactions), and reasoning traces (why decisions were made, enabling precedent lookup, compliance, and debugging). Knowledge graphs excel for memory because relationships are first-class, hop traversal is performant, graph embeddings like fastRP enable vector lookups, and algorithms like Louvain support community grouping. The Neo4j agent memory package is an open-source project integrating these three memory types into a context graph structure. A Lenny's Podcast demo shows how tools built on these APIs extract locations from episodes to build a navigable graph. Context graphs differ from traditional audit logs by capturing the why behind decisions. The architecture cycles: context graph retrieval informs the agent loop, which pushes results back into context memory. A financial services demo then concretizes this: a loan decision for Jessica Norris surfaces her bank account, related margin trades, a previous rejection, and fraud risk patterns, with graph traversal visible so the human making the final call can see what the system is drawing on. The open-source project pulls from a support ticket system, CRM, and internal business data via 10 MCP tools, using OpenAI embeddings to populate a Neo4j context graph with domain and reasoning graphs, exposed through a Next.js UI. Chin closes with resources: a new context graph course on GraphAcademy with a free Aura instance, and teases colleagues Zaid and ABK's deeper dive into agentic use cases.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction: The Trapped Engineer Problem
sections.summary: Stephen Chin introduces himself as head of developer relations at Neo4j. He frames the AI revolution as leaving engineers trapped — AI coding tools review their PRs and control them rather than the reverse, creating a limbo of amazing capabilities without human control.

sections.title: Blue Pill vs. Red Pill: Escaping the Matrix
sections.summary: Chin uses the Matrix metaphor: the blue pill means staying in a mire of siloed knowledge across Slack, customer threads, and enterprise systems where agents can't give good answers. The red pill means connecting all systems, decision traces, and tool calls for consolidated reasoning. Gartner officially added context graphs to the AI hype cycle; Foundation Capital posted about a $3 trillion startup opportunity.

sections.title: Knowledge Graphs and LLM Combination
sections.summary: Knowledge graphs hold nodes (people, things, companies), relationships, properties, and vector embeddings for similarity search. Combining LLM strengths (language, reasoning, creativity) with knowledge graph strengths (knowledge, context, enrichments) enables storing relationships, visualizing data, finding hidden patterns, and gaining insights to power context graph demos.

sections.title: Healthcare Example: Baseline vs. RAG vs. Graph RAG
sections.summary: Asking about Andre Jenkins' emphysema care plan: baseline LLM gives generic advice (prevent lung damage), vector RAG adds respiratory therapy and breathing exercises but remains generic, while graph RAG recommends medication management, smoking cessation counseling, and pulmonary rehabilitation — grounded in the patient's actual history of smoking and prior surgery. Key background information was lost in the similarity search.

sections.title: Three Memory Types for AI Agents
sections.summary: Beyond grounding with graph RAG, agents need memory: short-term (current pipeline state, conversation, activities), long-term (aggregated domain knowledge with good domain model for business processes and entities across interactions), and reasoning traces (why decisions were made, enabling precedent lookup, compliance, and debugging). LLMs typically return only results, not the reasoning behind them.

sections.title: Knowledge Graphs for Memory and Neo4j Agent Memory Package
sections.summary: Knowledge graphs are ideal for memory because relationships are first-class, hop traversal is performant, graph embeddings like fastRP enable vector lookups as entry points, and Louvain algorithm supports community grouping. LLMs can build Cypher queries. The open-source Neo4j agent memory package integrates short-term, long-term, and reasoning memory into a context graph structure.

sections.title: Lenny's Podcast Demo
sections.summary: An open-source demo built on Neo4j agent memory APIs loads all Lenny's Podcast episodes. It provides AI tools for accessing memory, extracting locations from episodes to build a navigable graph/map. The graph format provides a holistic view of the entire dataset that can be navigated and queried dynamically, unlike similarity search which returns only partial data.

sections.title: Context Graphs: Definition and Architecture
sections.summary: Context graphs solve cross-domain business problems by capturing the why — decision traces during model evaluation — organized by entities and relationships. Unlike traditional audit logs, they pull knowledge from Slack, emails, and informal conversations into a central queryable point. The architecture cycles: context graph retrieval informs the agent loop, which pushes results back into context memory for future queries.

sections.title: Financial Services Demo and Resources
sections.summary: A financial services application demonstrates context graphs for loan decisions. It models entities (people, organizations), events (decisions, transactions, approvals), and context (policies, risk factors, employee reasoning). The open-source project pulls from a support ticket system, CRM, and internal business data via 10 MCP tools, uses OpenAI embeddings to populate a Neo4j context graph with domain and reasoning graphs, and exposes a Next.js UI. Querying Jessica Norris for loan approval, the system surfaces her bank account, related margin trades, a previous rejection, and fraud detection patterns via visible graph traversal and Cypher queries. The AI recommends denying the loan with reasons and risk factors, giving humans the information needed to make and justify decisions. Chin closes with resources: a new context graph course on GraphAcademy with a free Aura instance, and teases colleagues Zaid and ABK's deeper dive into agentic use cases.
